"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4864: a dense, context-dependent signal with no simple reading.

What it does: predicts the component's typical activation, a constant -0.025, at every position.

Why: across 512 training rows (about 262k tokens) I could not find a short rule that tracks the
activation. Measured against the activation (std about 0.3):
- token identity (shrunk per-token means) explains about 0.5% of the variance;
- coarse token classes (digits, punctuation, spaces, words) explain essentially 0%;
- position in the document, repetition of earlier tokens, document-level averages,
  and the model's own next-token entropy or loss explain under 2%;
- the single hidden unit of layer 15's MLP with the same index, 4864, explains about 20%,
  but its value depends on context in a way I could not describe in words.
A constant at the mean is the simplest program that matches the component's average behaviour.
It scores about 0 variance explained, and switching the component off barely changes the model
(its KL is about 1.5e-6 nats per position either way).
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.025


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    return None, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Explanation of layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4865 (a single rank-one piece of the MLP down projection).

What the component does: it is almost inactive. Its causal importance is ~0 on every token
in the harvest corpus, and switching it off changes the model's next-token predictions by
almost nothing. Its activation is a small, diffuse readout of the MLP hidden state. It is
not explained by which token is present, nor by bracket depth or distance since a newline.

What this program predicts (the simple version): a rough average by position in the
document, with a bump on punctuation:
  - the first token of each document: about 0 (the activation there is essentially zero);
  - the next ~9 tokens of a document: higher on punctuation and newlines (~0.17) than on
    other tokens (~0.05);
  - later tokens: ~0.07 on punctuation and newlines, ~0.04 otherwise.

What it gets and what it misses: these are conditional means, so they are the best this kind
of rule can do, but they explain only about 0.2% of the activation's variance on training rows.
A per-token lookup table of mean activations would explain about 4% out of sample, but it is an
arbitrary table of token ids with no concept behind it, so it is not used here.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

EARLY_TOKENS = 10  # tokens after a document's first one counted as "early" in the document


def _is_punct(text):
    """Punctuation, or a token containing a newline."""
    return "\n" in text or regex.fullmatch(r"\s*[^\w\s]+\s*", text) is not None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # Position within the current document: resets where the document changes.
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n = 0
    else:
        n = carry[1] + 1
    if n == 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif n < EARLY_TOKENS:
        value = 0.165 if _is_punct(prefix.token_strings[-1]) else 0.053
    else:
        value = 0.07 if _is_punct(prefix.token_strings[-1]) else 0.036
    return (doc, n), value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4866 (component 4866 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj).

The component's input direction is almost entirely this one MLP hidden unit (weight
1.01; the next largest weight is 0.13), so its activation is that unit's value. The
unit is quiet almost everywhere and spikes negative on symbols that are glued onto the
word or number before them, with no space between:

- maths notation: a single-letter variable followed by an operator or digit, as in
  "x^2", "n+1", "a_1" (about -0.9 on average);
- a digit glued to a longer word, as in "CH2", "FAT3" (about -0.65), and an operator
  glued to one, as in "f'", "ab+" (about -0.36);
- identifier pieces joined by "_" or ".", such as "_range" or ".github" (about -0.27);
- the test-file suffix "_test" (as in "screen_test.go"), by far the strongest (about -9.4).

Prose, most digits and spaced-out symbols (weakly negative, about -0.2, not modelled
here) are left at zero. The spikes are rare and large, so these averages are rough:
this token-level rule explains a few percent of the variance (about 2% on training
text, 5% on the eval rows). Most of the variance sits in ordinary words and depends on
context this program cannot see.
"""

import re

READS = ()

SYMBOLS = set("+-−*/^_~=√²'\"`") | {"->"}
ALNUM_END = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]$")
LETTER_END = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]$")
SINGLE_LETTER_END = re.compile(r"(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])[A-Za-z]$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tok = cur.strip()
    same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    glued = bool(ALNUM_END.search(prev)) and not cur[:1].isspace()
    if tok == "_test":
        return carry, -9.4
    if glued and (tok in SYMBOLS or tok.isdigit()):
        if SINGLE_LETTER_END.search(prev):
            return carry, -0.9
        if tok in SYMBOLS:
            return carry, -0.36
        if LETTER_END.search(prev):
            return carry, -0.65
        return carry, 0.0
    if any(c.isalpha() for c in tok) and ("_" in tok or "." in tok):
        return carry, -0.27
    return carry, 0.0

"""Predict the component's average activation, with a rule for document boundaries.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4868 writes a small, diffuse signal
into the residual stream (activation std about 0.31, mean -0.05). Almost none of it is
explained by the visible text: the token identity, the previous token and the position
in the document each explain under 2% of its variance on held-out text.

The one clear pattern is at the special chat and document markers
(<|endoftext|>, <|im_start|>, <|im_end|>), where the activation is about -0.28 on
average. The first token of each document sits near 0. Everything else gets the
overall average, -0.05.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MARKERS = ("<|endoftext|>", "<|im_start|>", "<|im_end|>")
MARKER_VALUE = -0.28
OTHER_VALUE = -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    doc_start = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    if doc_start:
        return carry, 0.0
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] in MARKERS:
        return carry, MARKER_VALUE
    return carry, OTHER_VALUE

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4869 (the component's own neuron), read off the newest token.

The component is almost exactly this one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP (its
input direction is about 0.61 on that unit). Its activation is positive on
words of running English prose, most on plural nouns ("studies", "methods",
"techniques"), and also on acronyms and non-Latin text. It is slightly negative
on punctuation and brackets, where code and markup live. Its largest
values sit in methods-section prose, such as "as previously [described]" or
"performed with [software]", and its most negative values in formulaic
methods or ethics phrases ("were housed", "in accordance with").

This program only sees the newest token's shape, so it captures the broad
word-class trend and nothing finer. It explains under 1% of the variance
(eval: variance explained about 0.007, r about 0.08). Token identity, the
previous token, and document-level register each add almost nothing; the
activation is spread over many small contributions with no single word or
context behind them.
"""
import re

READS = ()

PLURAL_PROSE = re.compile(r" [a-z]+s")  # " studies", " methods"
PROSE_WORD = re.compile(r" [a-z]+")  # " the", " model"
CAPS = re.compile(r" ?[A-Z]{2,}")  # " PCR", "ROS"
CAPITAL_WORD = re.compile(r" [A-Z][a-z]+")  # " Smith"
NUMBER = re.compile(r" ?\d+")
PUNCT = re.compile(r"\s*[^\w\s]+\s*")  # punctuation and brackets, no letters


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if PLURAL_PROSE.fullmatch(s):
        value = 0.12
    elif PROSE_WORD.fullmatch(s):
        value = 0.065
    elif CAPS.fullmatch(s) or any(ord(c) > 127 for c in s):
        value = 0.055
    elif CAPITAL_WORD.fullmatch(s):
        value = 0.02
    elif NUMBER.fullmatch(s):
        value = 0.01
    elif PUNCT.fullmatch(s):
        value = 0.0
    else:
        value = 0.02
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4870: a dormant, context-driven component.

What it is: one rank-one direction written into the residual stream by the MLP of layer 15.
It almost never matters. Its causal importance is ~0 on every token (it never passes the
0.1 threshold on 10M tokens), and switching it off barely changes the model's next-token
predictions.

What its activation looks like: the first token of each document is always about 0. Every
other token has a small negative typical value (about -0.06), with a large, roughly symmetric
spread (std ~0.31) that no simple property of the token explains. Token identity, token class
(letters, digits, punctuation, CJK, whitespace) and position in the document together explain
essentially none of the variance out of sample.

So the program predicts the component's typical value: -0.06 on every token except the first
token of a document, where it predicts 0. This is the least-squares answer when nothing readable
predicts the spread. It captures the mean, not the variation.

Why the spread has no readable concept: the component is a dense direction over the layer-15 MLP
hidden units. The largest single unit (4870) carries about 30% of its variance, and it is signed
and diffuse: it is strongly negative and positive across ordinary prose, code and other text, with
no token or context class that it follows.

What a richer version would add: a shrunken per-token table explains about 2% of the variance
out of sample, at the cost of thousands of arbitrary token ids with no concept behind them.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL = -0.06
"""The component's mean activation over ordinary tokens in training rows."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # The first token of a document has no preceding context: the component reads about 0 there.
    first_of_document = prefix.position == 0 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    return carry, (0.0 if first_of_document else TYPICAL)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4871.

What it does, in plain terms: this component is a weak, diffuse direction in the
residual stream. Its activation is roughly zero-mean noise of size about 0.7, with
heavy tails, and almost none of that is explained by simple rules. Measured on
training text, the only clear regularities are two spots where the activation sits
well above its usual level:

  * the role word "assistant" right after the chat marker "<|im_start|>" (the start
    of a model turn), averaging about +4.8;
  * a "{\"" token that opens a line (the start of a JSON object, e.g. a tool call),
    averaging about +2.4.

The first token of each document is near zero. Everywhere else the program predicts
the component's typical value, about -0.03.

Switching the component off changes the model's output by almost nothing, so this
program is a description of where the activation is largest, not a mechanism.
"""

READS = ()

ROLE_MARK = "<|im_start|>"
ROLE_WORD = "assistant"
JSON_OPEN = '{"'
BASE = -0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if tok == ROLE_WORD and prev == ROLE_MARK:
        return carry, 4.8
    if tok == JSON_OPEN and prev.endswith("\n"):
        return carry, 2.4
    return carry, BASE

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 4872: a near-silent, unpredictable direction.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP output. It reads the MLP
hidden vector through V_c, which is dominated by hidden unit 4872 (weight 0.30) but
spreads over thousands of other units, and writes along U_c. Its activation has mean
about -0.027 and standard deviation 0.26, yet its contribution to the residual stream
is tiny (about 0.4% of the site's output RMS) and its causal importance is ~0 on every
token, so switching it off changes the model's predictions by almost nothing.

What the program does: it cannot reproduce the activation from the tokens. Across the
sampled text, token identity, previous token, character class, repetition, and position
within the row explain essentially none of its variance (out-of-sample R^2 below 0.01).
So the program predicts the component's typical value, -0.0268, at every position, except
the first token of each packed row, where the component reads about zero (that position
has no preceding context, and the activation there is ~0).

Why this simple version: a lookup table of token values would add a little variance on
paper but overfits and gives negative held-out R^2. Nothing conceptual is lost, because
the component carries almost no signal in the model's next-token predictions.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.0268  # the component's mean over the eval rows
ROW_START_ACTIVATION = 0.0  # the first token of a packed row reads ~0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return None, ROW_START_ACTIVATION
    return None, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4873: a diffuse, near-inert direction.

What it does: its activation (x . V_c) * ||U_c|| is a small signal with mean about
0.012 and standard deviation about 0.27, positive and negative in nearly equal measure.
No token identity, token class, script, or position rule explains it on held-out data
(lookup tables on token id, previous token id, script and document position all give
R^2 near 0). So the program predicts the typical value everywhere, and the one thing
it gets from the data is that the first token of each document sits near zero.

Why this is all it does: switching the component off changes the model's next-token
distribution by about 1e-6 nats per position, so there is no readable job for a
richer rule to recover. The only concentrated part of the activation is the MLP
hidden unit 4873 of the same layer (about 15% of the variance, with a large weight of
about 0.2), and that unit is polysemantic: its top contexts are next-word predictions
in unrelated text (for example "the person may be [interested]"), not one concept.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL = 0.012  # mean activation over ordinary tokens
FIRST = 0.005  # mean activation on a document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # A row packs documents end to end: a token starts a document if it is the row's
    # first token or its document label differs from the previous token's.
    starts_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, FIRST if starts_doc else TYPICAL


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Quick self-check on made-up labels: the first token of each document is FIRST.
    class _P:
        document_ids = [0, 0, 1]
        position = 2

    print(step(None, _P, {})[1])

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4874, read as a prose-sentence-end detector.

What it is: its activation is almost exactly MLP neuron 4874 of layer 15 (its
input vector is 0.86 on that unit and small elsewhere), scaled by a constant.
So the activation is positive where that neuron is on and negative where it is off.

What this program does, in plain terms:
- Predicts a high value at a sentence-ending mark (. ! ? and the CJK equivalents)
  that closes a long line of ordinary prose (10 or more English words since the
  last newline), a lower value at a short line-ending mark, a small positive
  value at commas, and a small positive value at a few clause-linking words
  ("but", "however", "therefore", "need", ...).
- Predicts about zero everywhere else.

This captures the broad pattern (sentence and clause ends in expository prose are
on, code, headings, lists and markup are off), but it explains only about 1% of the
variance of the activation: the neuron's value within each token class depends on
context that these rules do not see.
"""
import re

READS = ()

SENT_END = set(".!?。！？")
COMMA = set(",，、;:")
LINKERS = {"but", "however", "therefore", "thus", "so", "yet", "although",
           "because", "then", "need", "needs", "requires"}
PROSE_WORDS = 10


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    words = 0 if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    word = text.strip()
    value = 0.03
    if word in SENT_END:
        value = 0.5 if words >= PROSE_WORDS else 0.2
    elif word in COMMA:
        value = 0.12
    elif word.lower() in LINKERS:
        value = 0.15
    if "\n" in text:
        words = 0
    elif re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", word):
        words += 1
    return words, value

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 4875, as read by the down_proj component 4875.

The component's output is almost entirely that one MLP hidden unit: its input
direction puts weight 0.66 on unit 4875 and spreads the rest thinly, so its
activation is that unit's value times a fixed scale.

Surface behaviour: the activation is near 0 on most tokens, with rare large
swings (|value| > 3 on 0.1% of tokens). The strongest negatives fall mostly on a
later piece of a word split across tokens ('Stap|ling', 'faith|ful', '_H|ost',
'in|ik|lik'), where the model is finishing a word it has started. Large
positives are scattered over punctuation and short tokens.

This program keeps only the weak word-piece tendency: a token that continues
the word begun by the previous token (no space in between, both alphanumeric or
underscore) gets a small negative value; all other tokens get 0. Token identity,
token class, word depth and recent-token counts each explain under 1% of the
variance, so this rule explains almost none of it.
"""

READS = ()

CONTINUATION_VALUE = -0.013


def _word_char(s):
    return bool(s) and (s[0].isalnum() or s[0] == "_")


def _word_end(s):
    return bool(s) and (s[-1].isalnum() or s[-1] == "_")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    cur, prev = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if _word_char(cur) and _word_end(prev):
        return None, CONTINUATION_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""Units-of-measure detector for MLP neuron 4876 of layer 15.

This component is one hidden unit of layer 15's MLP (its read vector is the
unit basis vector, so its activation is that unit's value times the norm of
its write vector). It is near zero in most text and rises in quantitative
science writing: when the text names a unit of measure or a physical quantity
(kg, lbs, cubic, feet, volume, density, horsepower, per...). The unit's output
direction promotes words like "conversion", "volume", "unit" and "capacity".

This program predicts the activation from the words alone:
  - a large value when the current token is a unit or quantity word,
  - a smaller value for each such word among the 30 tokens before it in the
    same document.
It captures only a small part of the variance: most of the neuron's activity
is spread over ordinary positions that no word list explains.
"""
from collections import deque

READS = ()

UNITS = set("""
gram grams kg kilogram kilograms mg milligram lb lbs pound pounds oz ounce
ounces ton tons tonne cm mm km meter meters metre metres centimeter
millimeter kilometer inch inches ft feet foot yard yards mile miles acre acres
liter liters litre litres ml cc gallon gallons cup cups tsp tbsp pint quart
cubic sec second seconds min minute minutes hr hour hours joule joules mj kj
kwh kw watt watts horsepower hp calorie calories volt volts kv mah amp amps
ampere ohm ohms pa atm bar psi kelvin celsius fahrenheit mol mole moles molar
mph knot knots hz rpm
""".split())

QUANTITIES = set("""
mass weight volume density capacity area length distance speed velocity rate
pressure energy power temperature force acceleration frequency wavelength flow
thickness concentration per
""".split())

WINDOW = 30


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: the unit-or-quantity flags of the last WINDOW tokens of this document."""
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    recent = deque(maxlen=WINDOW) if new_doc or carry is None else deque(carry, maxlen=WINDOW)
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    flag = word in UNITS or word in QUANTITIES
    value = 0.02 + 0.6 * flag + 0.15 * sum(recent)
    recent.append(int(flag))
    return list(recent), value

"""Layer 15 MLP neuron 4877 (down_proj component 4877), as a weak heuristic.

What it does: this component is essentially one MLP hidden unit of layer 15,
so its activation is a signed, heavy-tailed number with mean about -0.015 and
std 0.46. Almost none of that variance follows a simple concept. Token identity,
previous token, document position, column, document type and repetition all
explain about 0 to 1 percent of it. The one signal we found is weak: at a
closing or separating token (")", ",", "):") that sits inside an open bracket,
the mean is about +0.08 (the activation is more often large and positive there,
e.g. the "row" in `for (...; row < rows; row++)` and the last argument of a
call or a parameter list). Everywhere else the mean is about -0.015.

So the program tracks bracket depth within each document, resetting at document
boundaries, and predicts +0.08 at a closer inside brackets and -0.015 elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

OPENERS = "([{"
CLOSERS = ")]}"
# Tokens that end an argument, parameter or loop-header item.
SEPARATORS = {",", ")", "):", "),", "):\n", ")\n"}
IN_BRACKET_VALUE = 0.08
ELSEWHERE_VALUE = -0.015


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (bracket depth so far, document of the last token), or None at a row's start.
    depth, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        depth = 0  # a new document: brackets from the last one no longer count
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    inside = depth > 0
    value = IN_BRACKET_VALUE if inside and s.strip() in SEPARATORS else ELSEWHERE_VALUE
    depth += sum(c in OPENERS for c in s) - sum(c in CLOSERS for c in s)
    return (max(depth, 0), prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""Component p-82af68dd layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4878, with a small baseline rule.

What the component is: nearly one hidden unit of layer 15's MLP. Its read
vector puts about half its squared norm on that unit (weight 0.76, the rest
spread thinly), so its activation is about 0.8 times the unit's value (gate
times up), scaled by its write norm 1.08. The value takes both signs, with
standard deviation 0.63 and heavy tails: about 6% of positions with
|activation| > 1 carry about two thirds of the variance.

What drives it: the context the attention layers have built up, not the
current token. On 8k training rows, the current token's identity explains
about 3% of the variance, and a bag of the previous 16 tokens adds under 1%.
A linear readout of the normalized residual entering the MLP reaches about
29% on held-out rows, but that direction is spread over many dimensions and
has no concept a reader can name.

What this program does: predicts a per-class mean from the current token's
characters. CJK characters are mildly negative, English words with a leading
space (mid-phrase) negative, English word pieces without a space and other
tokens mildly positive. It explains under 1% of the variance. It is an honest
baseline, not an account of the large spikes.
"""
import regex

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = s.strip()
    if regex.match(r"\p{Script=Han}", core):
        value = -0.11
    elif core.isascii() and core.isalpha():
        value = -0.05 if s[:1] == " " else 0.04
    else:
        value = 0.02
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 4879: a weak, mostly unpredictable readout.

What this component is: one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP output projection. It reads the
MLP hidden vector and mostly reads a single hidden unit (4879) plus a long tail of others, so
its activation is a dense, context-driven number with std about 0.3 and essentially no
token-level pattern. Its causal importance is ~0 everywhere, so switching it off barely
changes the model's predictions.

What this program does: it guesses the activation from the class of the token just read,
using the mean activation measured for each class on training text. Newlines and punctuation
sit a little above zero, mixed-script and some other tokens a little below; everything else is
near 0. This is the most a token-class rule can say: it explains well under 1% of the variance.
The context that really drives the activation (the residual stream at layer 15) is not
available to a program, so no simple rule reaches it.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Mean activation on training text, by the class of the newest token.
CLASS_MEAN = {
    "newline": 0.085,      # the token contains a line break
    "space": 0.047,        # whitespace only
    "punct": 0.054,        # punctuation and symbols
    "word": 0.022,         # an English word, with or without its leading space
    "other_script": 0.015,  # non-ASCII text (other scripts, emoji)
    "number": 0.003,       # digits
    "mixed": -0.013,       # anything else
    "empty": 0.0,          # a token that decodes to nothing (e.g. a partial byte sequence)
}


def token_class(text):
    if text == "":
        return "empty"
    if "\n" in text:
        return "newline"
    if text.isspace():
        return "space"
    if re.fullmatch(r" ?\d+", text):
        return "number"
    if re.fullmatch(r" ?[A-Za-z]+", text):
        return "word"
    if re.fullmatch(r" ?[^\x00-\x7f]+", text):
        return "other_script"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\W+", text):
        return "punct"
    return "mixed"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The activation at this position is predicted from the token read here, nothing before it.
    return carry, float(CLASS_MEAN[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])])

"""p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4881: a colon detector, strongest on message colons.

What it responds to (measured on training rows, 4096 rows, about 2M tokens):
- A colon ":" (or full-width "：") is the main trigger. Its activation averages about 3,
  and reaches 10 to 19 where the colon opens a printed message, status or error text,
  as in "Test Suites:", "error fetching addons:", "Failed to read config:" or a printf
  format. This program predicts the average colon value; it does not check message context.
- Exceptions, which are weaker: a colon right after a digit, as in a time (10:52) or
  a ratio (5:8), averages about 2; a colon right after a path, URL or "::" (src/index.ts:12,

    "together", "along", "combination", "conjunction", "completed", "finished", "replaced",
    "different", "distinct", "substitute", "compared", "rather",
}
# Words after which "of" is partitive ("most of", "majority of").
PARTITIVE = {

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4916: a weak detector for aligned, column-like text.

The component's activation is mostly near zero, with rare large positive spikes. The spikes
sit in layouts where runs of spaces pad items into columns (directory listings, tables,
aligned struct fields, indented code), and most sharply on a file-name extension (".js",
".sh", ".md", ".yaml", ".json", ".go", ...) that ends an item in such a listing, a few
tokens after the padding. The program predicts:

  * a baseline that rises with how much of the recent text (the previous 64 tokens of the
    document) is padding, a run of two or more spaces or tabs; and
  * a bonus of 4.5 when the current token is a file extension and padding appeared 2 to 12
    tokens back.

Everything else is predicted as about zero. On the eval rows this explains about 1.7% of
the activation's variance (correlation 0.14). Most of the variance is in spikes scattered
over many contexts that no short rule captures: on my training sample a per-token lookup
table reached only about 3%, and the token-level features tried (token class, repetition,
induction copies, column position) reached about 1% each. This is a partial reading, not a
full account of the component.
"""

import re
from collections import deque

READS = ()

WINDOW = 64  # tokens of recent context whose padding density is measured
NEAR = 12  # tokens back in which padding must appear for the extension bonus
DENSITY_WEIGHT = 2.0
EXTENSION_BONUS = 4.5
EXTENSION = re.compile(
    r"\.?(json|md|go|js|ts|py|yaml|yml|sh|txt|mod|sum|cjs|rs|cc|cpp|java|html|css|"
    r"toml|ini|bak|gz|xml|conf|sql)"
)


def is_padding(text):
    """A run of two or more spaces or tabs: the padding that aligns columns."""
    return len(text) >= 2 and text.strip() == ""


def is_extension(text):
    """A file-name extension, such as '.json' or 'js'."""
    return EXTENSION.fullmatch(text.strip().lower()) is not None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        carry = (document, deque(maxlen=WINDOW))  # a new document starts fresh
    _, recent = carry
    # recent holds (is_padding, is_extension) for the earlier tokens of this document
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(recent) == 0:
        density = 0.0
    else:
        density = sum(flag for flag, _ in recent) / len(recent)
    # padding 2 to NEAR tokens back (the token just before is excluded)
    near_padding = any(flag for flag, _ in list(recent)[-NEAR:-1])
    value = DENSITY_WEIGHT * density
    if is_extension(text) and near_padding:
        value += EXTENSION_BONUS
    recent.append((is_padding(text), is_extension(text)))
    return (document, recent), value

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.036  # the component's average over positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # A document's first token (where the model resets its context) sits near zero.
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4922: what down_proj component 4922 responds to.

The component reads mainly one MLP hidden unit (layer 15, unit 4922): its weight on that unit
is about 20 times its weight on any other unit. Its activation is near zero on most tokens and
very spiky on a few, and the spikes go both ways. The spikes sit mostly in base64-like strings
and in some English phrases, but their sign is not recoverable from the token or its word.

The only word-level signal this program uses is weak: activation dips negative on reflective or
'on closer look' wording (think, closer, sounds, seem, simple, actually, really) and rises on
interjections and certainty adverbs (Oh, Well, definitely, certainly, always, never). It predicts
those word means, the same for each occurrence, and 0 elsewhere. Scored on held-out rows it
explains about 0.2% of the activation's variance on eval rows. A full per-token mean table fitted
on other rows explained only about 1-2% in my held-out checks, so the component is close to
unpredictable from its tokens.
"""

READS = ()

# Reflective / 'on closer look' wording: negative activation.
REFLECTIVE = {
    " think": -0.5, " closer": -1.5, " closely": -0.9, " sounds": -2.5, " seem": -1.8,
    " simple": -0.7, " straightforward": -1.2, " carefully": -0.8, " actually": -0.9,
    " really": -0.7, " reality": -0.7,
}

# Interjections and certainty adverbs: positive activation.
EMPHATIC = {
    "Oh": 2.5, " Oh": 2.3, "Well": 1.3, " Well": 1.6, " Still": 1.1, " definitely": 1.1,
    " certainly": 1.0, " always": 0.8, " never": 0.7,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return carry, REFLECTIVE.get(word, EMPHATIC.get(word, 0.0))

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4923, seen through its down_proj component 4923.

What the component is: its input direction is almost exactly one MLP hidden unit of
layer 15 (weight 0.82 on that unit, about two thirds of its energy), so its activation
is that unit's value scaled by about 1.1. Its output pushes the next-token distribution
toward quantifier-like words ("each", "different", "various", "multiple", 各, 多种).

What is known about its activations: they are near zero on most tokens, with a heavy
tail (spikes up to about 14). The spikes lean toward prepositions that often introduce a
distribution or a quantity ("for", "from", "at", "in"), and toward the digits 0-2 in
codes and identifiers. Nothing simple explains most of the variance: no token class,
position, punctuation distance or internal norm does.

What this program does: predicts a small positive value on those prepositions and
digits, and zero everywhere else. It reads only the newest token, and it needs no state.
"""

READS = ()

# Prepositions that often come before a quantity or a distribution ("for each", "from various").
PREPOSITIONS = {" for", " from", " at", " in", " on", " to", " of", " by", " with", " into"}
DIGITS = {"0", "1", "2"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in {" for", " from", " at", " in"}:
        return carry, 0.3
    if token in PREPOSITIONS:
        return carry, 0.1
    if token in DIGITS:
        return carry, 0.1
    return carry, 0.0

"""A word-level guess at when component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4924 is active.

The component writes a direction that promotes next tokens meaning "free of charge"
("gratis", "无偿", "volunteered", "altruistic"). Its activation is most positive on
words about getting something without paying or working for it ("free", "gratis",
"without", "for nothing", "no effort"); it is moderately positive on money and cost
words ("cost", "fee", "profit", "payment") and on plain negations ("no", "not"), and
it runs higher through passages that are about money and cost than through others.
Its most negative values come from math and code text, which this program does not
model.

The program predicts: a strong value on free-of-charge words, a weaker value on money
and negation words, and a small extra value that follows how dense money words have
been in the current document so far (an exponentially decaying count, reset at each
document boundary). Everything else is zero.
"""

READS = ()

# Words meaning "without charge, payment or effort", in several languages.
FREE_OF_CHARGE = {
    "free", "gratis", "gratuit", "gratuito", "without", "nothing", "unpaid",
    "volunteer", "donation", "gift", "ohne", "sans", "без", "无偿", "免费", "無料",
}

# Money and cost words: the economic discourse the component leans into.
MONEY = {
    "money", "cost", "costs", "fee", "fees", "payment", "payments", "pay", "paid",
    "price", "profit", "profits", "compensation", "benefit", "benefits", "expense",
    "debt", "loan", "loans", "funds", "investment", "invest", "cheap", "expensive",
    "reward", "rewards", "effort", "consideration", "income", "salary", "wage",
    "dollar", "dollars", "budget", "tax", "taxes", "钱",
}

NEGATION = {"no", "not", "never", "none"}

DECAY = 0.95  # how fast the document's money density fades, per token
DENSITY_WEIGHT = 3.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    density = 0.0
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        density = carry[1]  # money density over this document's earlier tokens
    if word in FREE_OF_CHARGE:
        value = 1.5
    elif word in MONEY or word in NEGATION:
        value = 0.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    value += DENSITY_WEIGHT * density
    hit = 1.0 if word in FREE_OF_CHARGE or word in MONEY else 0.0
    return (doc, DECAY * density + (1 - DECAY) * hit), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4926: a diffuse, context-driven direction.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP output. It reads the MLP
hidden state through one input direction V_c and writes along one output direction
U_c. Its activation is (hidden · V_c) * ||U_c||. The input direction puts its largest
weight on hidden unit 4926 (0.33 of the direction's norm 0.80, about 17% of its squared
norm), but the rest is spread over thousands of other units, so no single neuron or
word explains the activation.

What this program does: it predicts the activation from position in the document
alone, which is the only simple feature that carries any signal:
  - the first token of each document is about 0;
  - the second token is somewhat negative (mean about -0.13);
  - every later token sits near the component's mean value, about +0.08.

What it does not capture: token identity, character class (CJK, digits, punctuation,
whitespace), local context and document topic each explain about 1% or less of the
variance on held-out training rows, so they are left out. The variance this program
explains is therefore close to zero. Its value is that it is short and honest about
the component's behaviour.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN = 0.08  # the component's typical activation at an ordinary position
FIRST = 0.0  # document's first token
SECOND = -0.13  # document's second token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label of the previous token, index of the previous token within its document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        k = 0  # first token of a new document
    else:
        k = carry[1] + 1
    if k == 0:
        value = FIRST
    elif k == 1:
        value = SECOND
    else:
        value = MEAN
    return (doc, k), float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4927 (component 4927 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj).

What the component is: a single rank-one readout of the layer-15 MLP hidden state. Its
input direction is dominated by the hidden unit 4927 itself (more than half of its squared
norm), so its activation is mostly that unit's value (a SiLU-gated product, signed) times
the norm of the unit's output column. That unit's own value correlates with the activation
at r = 0.54 (about 30% of variance), and the rest is a diffuse sum over other hidden units.

What this program does: it predicts the activation with the only structure found that is
simple to state. The first token of every document is ~0 (its activation there is
essentially zero), and every other token sits at the typical small negative value, the
mean of the non-start tokens (about -0.023). It does not model the large, rare excursions
(|activation| > 2 on about 0.2% of tokens, carrying about 17% of the variance): no word,
token class, script, position, repetition or word-frequency rule we tried predicts them,
and the token identity alone explains about 1.5% of the variance.

Why it is this simple: the component's contribution is tiny (RMS about 0.5% of the site's
output) and it never passes the causal-importance threshold, so switching it off changes
the model's output by almost nothing. The program is an honest baseline, not a mechanism.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL_VALUE = -0.023
"""The activation's mean away from a document's first token."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # A document's first token: its activation is ~0 there.
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else TYPICAL_VALUE
